Short answer: Start with four boring jobs: strong logins, updates, backups, and a plan for suspicious messages. You do not need a movie hacker dashboard.

What this means for your business

Your email, payment account, domain, booking tool, and file storage are the keys to the shop. Protect those first. A giant security shopping list can wait.

What to watch

  • Shared passwords or one password used everywhere.
  • Old staff accounts that still work.
  • Updates postponed on the register, router, or office computer.
  • A backup nobody has tested.

Do this next

  1. List the five accounts that could stop business today.
  2. Turn on multifactor authentication, starting with email and banking.
  3. Remove old users and update the devices that take money.
  4. Back up one important folder, then prove you can restore a file.

When Little Fight fits

Call us when the list is messy, a device keeps failing, or nobody knows who owns the accounts. If there may be an active breach, stop changing things and contact a qualified incident-response professional.
